I will still do it the way that has kept my family steady: I start from what I used last year, then I move a little if I think the field needs it. On my 12 mu, I will keep most land in wheat-maize because that is the sure road here, and I will leave a smaller piece for cotton so I do not put everything in one basket. I have a well, so I am not as scared of dry spells, and with water in hand I do not want to save too hard on fertilizer and lose yield. Around here, if wheat looks weak after turning green, people add another round of urea, and I do the same. Maize eats hard in summer, so I feed it more than wheat, and I would rather give a bit extra than watch the leaves go pale. Cotton I will not plant too much, because it takes more watching and more sprays, but I will keep some because if the price is decent it still brings money. I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen neighbors get a fuller stand and better harvest. For tillage, I will plough before wheat and cotton if the ground is hard, and after wheat I will mostly use rotary tillage for maize so I can move fast in the tight season.
